subject: Computer Networking
title: Asymmetric Encryption
description: A micro-lesson that makes Asymmetric Encryption usable.

hook.text: What if you could lock a box with one key and only a different key could open it? That's asymmetric encryption.

buildup.text: You have a public key anyone can use to encrypt messages to you. Only your private key can decrypt them.

discovery.text: RSA and ECC are common algorithms. They rely on math problems that are easy one way but nearly impossible to reverse.

twist.text: Asymmetric encryption is slow — about 1,000 times slower than AES. It's used for key exchange, not bulk data.

climax.text: TLS uses asymmetric crypto to exchange a symmetric key securely. Then the fast symmetric key handles the actual data.

punchline.text: Two keys: one public, one private. No shared secret needed.

quiz.question: Why isn't asymmetric encryption used for all data?
options: It's much slower than symmetric encryption
It's less secure than symmetric encryption
It can only work over local networks

details.summary: Asymmetric encryption uses a mathematically linked key pair: a public key that anyone can use to encrypt data, and a private key that only the owner can use to decrypt it. This solves the key distribution problem of symmetric encryption and enables digital signatures and secure key exchange.
details.whyItMatters: Asymmetric encryption makes secure communication possible between parties who have never met. It underpins TLS, SSH, email encryption, and cryptocurrency — the foundation of online trust.
takeaways: Public keys encrypt; only the matching private key can decrypt
RSA and elliptic curve are the dominant asymmetric algorithms
Asymmetric encryption is slower than symmetric, used for key exchange

faq.question: How do public and private keys work together?
faq.answer: Anyone can encrypt a message with your public key, but only your private key can decrypt it. Conversely, you can sign data with your private key, and anyone with your public key can verify the signature came from you. This duality enables both confidentiality and authentication.

faq.question: Why not use asymmetric encryption for everything?
faq.answer: Asymmetric encryption is about 1,000 times slower than symmetric encryption. In practice, asymmetric encryption securely exchanges a symmetric key, then symmetric encryption handles the actual data.
